propositions.text: Applicant seeks judicial review of visa officer's refusal of permanent residence application under Skilled Worker category due to inadmissibility under IRPA.
propositions.quote: Mr. Mahmoud Hoseinnejad Asl is seeking judicial review of a visa officer’s decision refusing his application for permanent residence under the Skilled Worker category, on the basis that he is inadmissible pursuant to paragraphs 40(1)(a) and 40(2)(a) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, SC 2001, c 27 [IRPA].

propositions.text: Applicant found to have made material misrepresentation by providing a non-genuine employer reference letter.
propositions.quote: The Applicant was found to have made a material misrepresentation by providing the visa officer with a letter of reference that was not genuine and that was not from his employer.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant seeks judicial review of visa officer's refusal due to inadmissibility for material misrepresentation via a non-genuine employer reference letter, court states.

propositions.text: Applicant is Iranian citizen who applied for permanent residence in May 2013 under Skilled Worker class including his wife.
propositions.quote: The Applicant is a citizen of Iran. In May 2013, he submitted an application for permanent residence in Canada under the Skilled Worker class. He included his wife in his application.

propositions.text: Applicant intended to work as civil engineer, holds Master's in Architectural Engineering, worked at AWQAF since 2008 and previously at Khesht o Naghsh Markazi Co.
propositions.quote: The Applicant intended to work as a civil engineer in Canada. He has a Master’s Degree in Architectural Engineering from the Iran University of Science and Technology in Tehran and, since July 2008, he has worked as a construction engineer at the Endowments and Charity Affairs Organization [AWQAF]. Previously, he worked as a construction engineer for Khesht o Naghsh Markazi Co, from March 2004 to December 2005, and from August 2007 to July 2008.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant is Iranian citizen who applied for permanent residence with wife, intending to work as civil engineer with relevant education and work history, court states.

propositions.text: Applicant submitted job documentation including employer reference letter and responded to embassy's request with updated job certificate.
propositions.quote: In his application for permanent residence, the Applicant submitted documentation to describe his job and duties at AWQAF, including a reference letter from the employer detailing the duties performed, as well as documentation regarding other related work experience. On April 16, 2014, the Canadian Embassy in Warsaw, Poland requested a medical examination and additional documents from the Applicant. He replied on May 21, 2014, with additional supporting documents including an updated Job Certificate from AWQAF, dated April 27, 2014, once again outlining his occupational duties.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant submitted job documentation including employer reference letter and updated job certificate responding to embassy's request, court states.

propositions.text: Visa officer contacted AWQAF personnel who said Applicant worked there but reference letter was not genuine or issued by AWQAF.
propositions.quote: The visa officer was advised that although the Applicant worked at AWQAF, the reference letter was not genuine and was not issued by AWQAF.

propositions.text: GCMS entry states Applicant works there but submitted work reference letter is not genuine and not issued by AWQAF.
propositions.quote: Was advised that although [the Applicant] is working there, work reference letter submitted by him is not genuine and was not issued by this organization.

paragraphs.summary: Visa officer contacted AWQAF who confirmed Applicant worked there but reference letter was not genuine, earlier decision-maker found, court states.

propositions.text: Applicant emailed visa officer explaining AWQAF prohibits communication with foreign countries without embassy in Iran, so HR managers cannot respond to fax inquiry.
propositions.quote: [AWQAF] is a public organization governed by hardliners and unfortunately in such public organizations a proclamation was strictly issued prohibiting any kind of communication with foreign countries without embassy in Iran. Therefore, the international affairs or human resource managers are not allowed to respond to your fax inquiry.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant emailed visa officer explaining AWQAF prohibits communication with foreign countries without embassy, so HR cannot respond to fax inquiry, applicant says.

propositions.text: Unclear if Applicant knew of officer's conversation with AWQAF representative at this time.
propositions.quote: It is not clear whether the Applicant was aware of the officer’s conversation with a representative of AWQAF at this time.

propositions.text: Applicant offered to connect officer with his direct manager and said he did not inform AWQAF of immigration plans to avoid job risk; work reference addressed to local company.
propositions.quote: In the email, the Applicant offered to facilitate the visa officer’s connection with his direct manager, in charge of the “Engineering Department”, and also asked whether he could assist by providing further documentation. He indicated that he had not advised AWQAF of his intention to immigrate to Canada, because this would put his job at risk. He explained that his “work reference” had therefore been addressed to a local company in Iran.

paragraphs.summary: Unclear if Applicant knew of officer's AWQAF contact; Applicant offered to connect officer with manager and said work reference addressed to local company to protect job, applicant says.

propositions.text: Visa officer sent procedural fairness letter stating belief Applicant deliberately misled by submitting non-genuine work reference letter, considering inadmissibility for misrepresentation under IRPA.
propositions.quote: In an attempt to verify the authenticity of your work reference letter, I contacted [AWQAF] in Iran and I was advised that the work reference letter which was submitted by you was not genuine and was not issued by this organization. Therefore, it is my belief that you have deliberately tried to mislead me in a relevant matter which could induce an error in the administration of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and I am considering recommending to my supervisor that you be found inadmissible to Canada for misrepresentation pursuant to subsection 40(1)(a) of the Act.

propositions.text: Applicant given 30 days to respond in writing to concerns raised in procedural fairness letter.
propositions.quote: You have 30 days from the date of this letter to respond in writing to my concerns as noted above.

paragraphs.summary: Visa officer sent procedural fairness letter alleging deliberate misrepresentation via non-genuine reference letter and gave Applicant 30 days to respond, earlier decision-maker states.

propositions.text: Applicant responded to procedural fairness letter stating HR manager said they cannot verify work reference and job certificate was issued to local company, not allowed to send to Canadian embassy.
propositions.quote: He thereby stated that the human resources manager at AWQAF had told him that “we are not allowed to verify your work reference in response and furthermore your job certificate was issued to a local company and you were not permitted to send it to Canadian embassy”.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant responded to procedural fairness letter saying HR manager said they cannot verify work reference and job certificate was issued to local company, applicant says.

propositions.text: Applicant explained work reference originally addressed to Canpars, later deleted addressee to submit for immigration without employer's knowledge.
propositions.quote: The Applicant further explained that his work reference had originally been addressed to Canpars, the local company to which the Applicant had referred to in his previous email. However, he had subsequently deleted Canpars as the addressee in order to submit the reference letter for immigration purposes, without the knowledge of his employer.

propositions.text: Attached translated letter from Canpars confirmed receipt of job certificate addressed to it dated April 27, 2014.
propositions.quote: The attached translated letter from Canpars confirmed that the company had received the Applicant’s Job Certificate addressed to it, dated April 27, 2014.

propositions.text: Attached letter from translation bureau explained Iranian public organizations forbid issuing job certificates to foreign countries without embassy; letters usually addressed to local company; translations often delete addressees.
propositions.quote: According to strict rules come into force in most of Iranian public organizations, issuance of personnel’s job certificate to foreign countries without embassy in Iran is forbidden, so these letters are usually issued addressing a local company. Also for immigration purposes, the content of the letter it [sic] more important than the receiver then it is common that official translation bureau usually delete the receivers of letters.

propositions.text: Applicant requested translation office to modify letter to delete addressee for immigration purposes.
propositions.quote: Considering all this point, Mahmoud Hosinnejad [sic] Asl requested the translation office for necessary modifications and the newly formatted letter bearing the addressed company (Canpars Company) that is attached.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant explained work reference was originally addressed to Canpars, deleted addressee for immigration without employer's knowledge, attached confirming letter and translation bureau's explanation, applicant says.

propositions.text: Applicant provided additional AWQAF documents: social insurance, contract, salary slips, affidavits, customer letters, personnel cards, job title table, and organization chart.
propositions.quote: Other additional AWQAF documentation provided by the Applicant were: a social insurance document; an employee contract; salary slips; an affidavit of three of the Applicant’s colleagues, swearing they work with him; customers’ letters from the Department General of Technical Supervision verifying the Applicant’s position; the Applicant’s personnel card and those of three of his colleagues; a job title table of people working at the Department General and the position of the Applicant himself; and an organization chart.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant provided additional AWQAF documents including social insurance, contract, salary slips, affidavits, customer letters, personnel cards, job title table, and organization chart, applicant says.

propositions.text: Applicant sent letter reiterating position, attached job certificate from new HR manager less strict, suggested verifying reference via Italian or Norwegian Embassy due to government prohibition.
propositions.quote: The Applicant suggested that the officer verify his work reference through either the Italian or Norwegian Embassy in Tehran, given the government proclamation prohibiting companies like AWQAF from providing any response to communications from a country without an embassy in Iran.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant reiterated position, attached job certificate from new HR manager, suggested verifying reference via Italian or Norwegian Embassy due to government prohibition, applicant says.

propositions.text: Visa officer found Applicant inadmissible for misrepresentation under IRPA paragraph 40(1)(a) for misrepresenting employment experience.
propositions.quote: The visa officer found that the Applicant was “inadmissible for misrepresentation for directly or indirectly misrepresenting or withholding material facts relating to a relevant matter that induces or could induce an error in the administration of this Act”, pursuant to paragraph 40(1)(a) of the IRPA.

propositions.text: Officer based decision on AWQAF's inability to confirm genuineness of employment references, leading to inadmissibility for five years under paragraph 40(2)(a).
propositions.quote: The visa officer stated that he reached this determination on the basis that AWQAF had been unable to confirm the genuineness of the Applicant’s employment references; thus, the Applicant had provided an inaccurate account of his employment experience history. He would accordingly be inadmissible for five years following this determination, by virtue of paragraph 40(2)(a) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: Visa officer found Applicant inadmissible for misrepresentation due to unconfirmed employment references, imposing five-year inadmissibility, earlier decision-maker states.

propositions.text: GCMS notes show officer reviewed Applicant's response but remained concerned as employer did not confirm genuineness of references.
propositions.quote: information provided failed to disabuse me of my concerns regarding this application. The fact is that the [Applicant’s] employer did not confirm the genuineness of the work references submitted by [him].

propositions.text: Officer uncertain of Applicant's work capacity and whether experience meets requirements due to non-genuine references.
propositions.quote: Although [he] might be working for this employer, in light of submission of references which are not genuine, it is not certain in what capacity he is working and whether his work experience meets the minimum requirements and Ministerial Instructions.

propositions.text: Officer noted prior verifications in Iran found no issues raised by Applicant's claims.
propositions.quote: This office has conducted numerous verifications in Iran, including with state institutions such as judiciary institutions, universities, etc. and none of the issues raised by the [A]pplicant were noted.

paragraphs.summary: GCMS notes show officer remained concerned as employer did not confirm genuine references; prior verifications found no issues, earlier decision-maker states.

propositions.text: Officer found Applicant's response did not disabuse concerns and concluded on balance of probabilities Applicant lacks claimed employment experience.
propositions.quote: The response from the client has not disabused me of the concerns raised. In my opinion, on a balance of probabilities, I find it reasonable to conclude that the applicant does not have the stated employment experience as claimed.

paragraphs.summary: Officer concluded Applicant's response did not remove concerns and found Applicant likely lacks claimed employment experience, earlier decision-maker states.

propositions.text: Issues: Did officer err in finding misrepresentation? Did officer err by not disclosing extrinsic evidence or not providing opportunity to address it?
propositions.quote: This application for judicial review raises the following issues: A. Did the officer err in finding that the Applicant misrepresented his employment experience? B. Did the officer err by not disclosing extrinsic evidence to the Applicant and/or by not providing him with an opportunity to address that extrinsic evidence?

paragraphs.summary: Court identifies issues: whether officer erred in finding misrepresentation and in handling extrinsic evidence disclosure and opportunity to respond.

propositions.text: Finding of misrepresentation is mixed fact and law, reviewable on reasonableness standard.
propositions.quote: The first question is a question of mixed fact and law, and is reviewable on the standard of reasonableness (Seraj v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2016 FC 38 at para 11; Singh v Canada, 2015 FC 377 at para 12; Karami v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2009 FC 788 at para 14).

paragraphs.summary: Court states misrepresentation finding is mixed fact and law, reviewed on reasonableness standard.

propositions.text: Issues of extrinsic evidence disclosure and procedural fairness are questions of procedural fairness, reviewed on correctness standard.
propositions.quote: As to the second question, issues relating to extrinsic evidence and its disclosure are questions of procedural fairness, and are reviewable on the standard of correctness (Qureshi v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2009 FC 1081 at para 14; Dios v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2008 FC 1322 at para 23).

paragraphs.summary: Court states extrinsic evidence disclosure and procedural fairness issues are reviewed on correctness standard.

propositions.text: Applicant argues officer ignored multiple pieces of evidence.
propositions.quote: I do not agree with the Applicant that the officer ignored multiple pieces of evidence.

propositions.text: Decision-makers not required to refer to every piece of evidence (Cepeda-Gutierrez v Canada).
propositions.quote: As acknowledged by the parties, decision-makers are not required to refer to every piece of evidence (Cepeda-Gutierrez v Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) (1998), 157 FTR 35 at para 16).

propositions.text: Reviewing court presumes tribunal considered entire record; applicant bears high burden to prove otherwise (Herrera Andrade v Canada).
propositions.quote: In Herrera Andrade v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2012 FC 1490 at paragraph 11, Justice Gleason held that “the starting point for the inquiry in respect of an argument regarding the impact of failure to mention key evidence is that the reviewing court must presume that the tribunal considered the entire record”, and thus the Applicant “bear[s] a high burden of persuasion”.

propositions.text: Court must assess both outcome and reasons of tribunal in reasonableness review (Newfoundland and Labrador Nurses’ Union v Newfoundland and Labrador).
propositions.quote: Second, in assessing reasonableness, the Court must assess both the outcome and the reasons of the tribunal, as per Newfoundland and Labrador Nurses’ Union v Newfoundland and Labrador (Treasury Board), 2011 SCC 62 at paragraph 14.

propositions.text: Deference given to tribunal's findings, especially on matters within expertise.
propositions.quote: Third, the Court must give deference to the tribunal’s findings, especially where such findings are at the core of the tribunal’s expertise.

paragraphs.summary: Court rejects Applicant's claim officer ignored evidence, citing case law on evidence consideration, burden, reasonableness review, and deference to tribunal expertise.

propositions.text: Failure to analyze contrary evidence does not necessarily make decision unreasonable (Andrade).
propositions.quote: Andrade, above at paragraph 9, holds that Cepeda-Gutierrez “does not stand for the proposition that failure to analyze evidence that runs contrary to a tribunal's conclusion necessarily renders a decision unreasonable”.

propositions.text: Decision overturned only if omitted evidence is critical, contradicts conclusion, and tribunal failed to consider material.
propositions.quote: Instead, a decision will only be overturned in circumstances “where the non-mentioned evidence is critical, contradicts the tribunal’s conclusion and the reviewing court determines that its omission means that the tribunal did not have regard to the material before it”.

propositions.text: High bar for finding decision unreasonable due to omitted evidence.
propositions.quote: Thus, the bar for finding that the decision is unreasonable is high.

paragraphs.summary: Court explains failure to analyze contrary evidence does not necessarily make decision unreasonable; high bar to overturn for omitted critical evidence, citing Andrade.

propositions.text: Applicant has not met high bar to show decision unreasonable due to omitted evidence.
propositions.quote: The Applicant has not convinced me that this bar is reached in this case.

propositions.text: Officer considered Applicant's documents but remained concerned that AWQAF said reference letter was not genuine.
propositions.quote: The officer considered the supporting documents submitted by the Applicant, as well as the job certificate, and found that these documents had not disabused him of his original concerns, i.e. that a representative from AWQAF stated that the Applicant’s reference letter was not genuine and was not issued by AWQAF.

propositions.text: Subsequent documents did not change officer's view that original reference letter was fraudulent.
propositions.quote: The subsequent documentation provided by the Applicant simply did not change the officer’s mind that the original reference letter was fraudulent.

propositions.text: Applicant did not provide evidence of being targeted by hardliners, which could have supported claim about AWQAF's refusal to verify letter.
propositions.quote: Moreover, I agree with the Respondent that the Applicant did not provide evidence that he was targeted by hardliners. Such evidence could have helped substantiate his claim that the AWQAF representative told the officer his letter was not genuine because of the purported government proclamation.

propositions.text: Translation bureau letter stated proclamation in effect but did not state AWQAF was subject to it.
propositions.quote: The Applicant did provide the letter from the Pendar Official Translation Bureau stating that such a proclamation was in effect, but it did not state that AWQAF was subject to it.

propositions.text: Officer successfully contacted AWQAF and confirmed Applicant worked there.
propositions.quote: In any event, the officer was able to successfully contact AWQAF and the person contacted did confirm that the Applicant worked there.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Applicant did not meet high bar to show decision unreasonable; officer considered documents but remained concerned about fraudulent letter; no evidence of targeting by hardliners; AWQAF confirmed employment.

propositions.text: A finding of inadmissibility due to misrepresentation requires clear and convincing evidence.
propositions.quote: a finding of inadmissibility due to misrepresentation is a serious one, and that it must be made with “clear and convincing” evidence

propositions.text: The AWQAF representative's statement was clear and convincing that the reference letter was not genuine or issued by AWQAF.
propositions.quote: I find that the statement from the AWQAF representative to the officer was clear and convincing to the effect that the reference letter was neither genuine, nor issued by AWQAF.

propositions.text: The Applicant did not prove otherwise regarding the genuineness of the reference letter.
propositions.quote: The Applicant did not discharge his burden of proving otherwise.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds clear and convincing evidence that the reference letter was not genuine and the applicant failed to prove otherwise.

propositions.text: Procedural fairness adherence is evaluated for extrinsic evidence questions without a standard of review.
propositions.quote: this Court has held that it is not necessary to discuss the standard of review, but that it should evaluate whether the rules of procedural fairness have been adhered to

propositions.text: For other procedural fairness questions, the standard of review is correctness.
propositions.quote: For other questions of procedural fairness, the standard of review is correctness

propositions.text: The officer did not breach procedural fairness in this case.
propositions.quote: I find that the officer did not breach procedural fairness.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains the standard of review for procedural fairness and finds no breach by the officer.

propositions.text: Procedural fairness owed by visa officers is minimal but requires informing applicants of concerns.
propositions.quote: the procedural fairness owed by visa officers is on the low end of the spectrum...require[s] visa officers to inform applicants of their concerns

paragraphs.summary: The court states visa officers owe minimal procedural fairness but must inform applicants of concerns.

propositions.text: The officer sent a procedural fairness letter after contacting AWQAF, stating the reference letter was not genuine.
propositions.quote: The officer provided the Applicant with a procedural fairness letter...the representative advised him that the reference letter was not genuine

propositions.text: The letter made clear the applicant had to address the concern of misrepresentation.
propositions.quote: the letter made it clear that this was the concern that the Applicant had to address

propositions.text: The onus is on the applicant to demonstrate no misrepresentation occurred.
propositions.quote: the onus was on the Applicant to demonstrate that no misrepresentation occurred

paragraphs.summary: The officer sent a procedural fairness letter stating the reference letter was not genuine and the applicant had to address this concern.

propositions.text: The question of Iranian companies' communication with foreign authorities was not an officer concern.
propositions.quote: The question of whether Iranian companies respond to foreign authorities did not form part of the officer’s concerns

propositions.text: Applicant was advised of officer's communication with AWQAF and had opportunity to address concerns later.
propositions.quote: he was advised of it in the procedural fairness letter a few weeks later, and had an opportunity to fully address it then

propositions.text: Applicant did not provide evidence that Iranian companies cannot communicate with foreign authorities.
propositions.quote: He did not do so.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the officer's communication with AWQAF was known to the applicant who failed to provide evidence about Iranian companies' communication issues.

propositions.text: GCMS notes about Canadian Embassy contacting Iranian companies corroborate officer's verification with AWQAF.
propositions.quote: The officer’s statement in the GCMS notes that the Canadian Embassy has successfully contacted other Iranian companies in the past only corroborated his own successful verification attempt with AWQAF.

propositions.text: This does not constitute extrinsic evidence but general knowledge forming part of officer's expertise.
propositions.quote: I am not convinced that this constitutes extrinsic evidence, as the Applicant asserts. Rather, it is simply general knowledge which forms part of the officer’s expertise.

propositions.text: Applicants must make a convincing case; officers use general knowledge without necessarily disclosing concerns.
propositions.quote: visa officers will use their general experience and knowledge of local conditions to draw inferences and reach conclusions...without necessarily putting any concerns that may arise to the applicant

propositions.text: The onus is on the applicant to ensure the application is comprehensive and convincing.
propositions.quote: The onus is upon the applicant to ensure that the application is comprehensive and contains all that is needed to make a convincing case.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds GCMS notes are general knowledge, not extrinsic evidence, and applicants must make a convincing case with comprehensive applications.

propositions.text: Applicant knew of officer's communication with AWQAF and could have addressed concerns with evidence.
propositions.quote: the Applicant did know about the officer’s communication with AWQAF...he could have addressed this with evidence

propositions.text: Applicant was given reasonable opportunity to present his case.
propositions.quote: He was given a reasonable opportunity to present his case

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the applicant knew of the communication and had a reasonable opportunity to respond with evidence.

propositions.text: Officers are not required to disclose extrinsic evidence reasonably anticipated by the applicant.
propositions.quote: officers are not required to disclose extrinsic evidence where the applicant could reasonably anticipate that it would be consulted

propositions.text: It was reasonable to anticipate officer's use of general knowledge including past communications with Iranian companies.
propositions.quote: it was reasonable to anticipate that the officer would refer to his general knowledge and that this would include knowledge of past interactions or communications between the Canadian Embassy and Iranian companies

paragraphs.summary: The court finds officers need not disclose extrinsic evidence reasonably anticipated by applicants, including general knowledge of past communications.

propositions.text: Even if procedural fairness was breached, the decision would stand as the breach would not change the outcome.
propositions.quote: even if the officer breached procedural fairness by not disclosing extrinsic evidence...the breach would not have changed the outcome

propositions.text: Officer's decision was based on successful contact with AWQAF and fraudulent letter information.
propositions.quote: Since the officer successfully contacted AWQAF, and obtained the information about the fraudulent letter from that phone call, he could have reached his decision without the knowledge of the Canadian Embassy’s previous contacts

paragraphs.summary: The court finds any procedural fairness breach would not affect the decision, which was based on direct contact with AWQAF.

propositions.text: Officer did not breach procedural fairness by not disclosing AWQAF confirmation of applicant's employment.
propositions.quote: I cannot agree...the officer clearly expressed the issue in the procedural fairness letter: he was concerned that the reference letter was fraudulent

propositions.text: Applicant's employment confirmation does not negate concern about fraudulent reference letter.
propositions.quote: Even if the officer believed that the Applicant worked at AWQAF, this did not change the fact that the Applicant could provide a fraudulent reference letter from that employer

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no breach in not disclosing employment confirmation, as the concern was the fraudulent reference letter.

propositions.text: Applicant had opportunity to respond but failed to prove the reference letter was truthful.
propositions.quote: The Applicant had the opportunity to respond to the officer’s concerns, and failed to discharge his burden of proving otherwise

propositions.text: Applicant could have provided sworn evidence from the letter's author but did not.
propositions.quote: he could have provided sworn evidence from the author of the reference letter attesting that it was truthful. He did not do so

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the applicant failed to prove the reference letter's truth despite opportunity and could have provided sworn evidence.

propositions.text: The application for judicial review is dismissed.
propositions.quote: This application for judicial review is dismissed.

propositions.text: No question of general importance is certified.
propositions.quote: No question of general importance is certified

propositions.text: No costs are granted.
propositions.quote: No costs are granted

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the judicial review, certifies no question of general importance, and grants no costs.
